sources.entry: ryot - Track various facets of your life - media, fitness, etc. (Demo) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Ryot is a self-hosted tracker for media consumption (books, shows, games, etc.) and fitness activities, run as a Docker stack with PostgreSQL.
summary.what_it_does: Ryot tracks media such as movies, TV shows, anime, manga, books, audiobooks, podcasts, music and video games, along with workouts and body measurements. It can import history from Goodreads, Trakt, MyAnimeList and Audiobookshelf, and automatically track activity via Jellyfin, Plex, Kodi and Emby integrations. Fitness features include logging workouts against an exercise database, tracking body measurements over time, and viewing progress graphs. On the technical side it offers OpenID Connect login, notifications via Discord, Ntfy and Apprise, a GraphQL API, and PWA support. The README says the core is written in Rust. A separate paid Pro version adds profile sharing, recommendations and collections.
use_cases: track books, shows and games I consume
import history from Goodreads or Trakt
auto-track watching from Jellyfin or Plex
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with a postgres:18-alpine service (ryot-db) and an ignisda/ryot:v10 service on port 8000
Set SERVER_ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN to a long random string
Open the web UI on port 8000 in a browser
For production setups, follow the installation guide linked in the README
notable: Tracks both media consumption and fitness (workouts, body measurements) in one app
Automatic tracking through Jellyfin, Plex, Kodi and Emby integrations
Imports from Goodreads, Trakt, MyAnimeList and Audiobookshelf
GraphQL API and OpenID Connect login for custom setups
Live demo available; demo data resets every 24 hours
caveats: Some features (profile sharing, personalized recommendations, collections) are only in the paid Pro version
Upgrading from v9 requires following a separate migration guide
The quick start uses placeholder database credentials and a token that must be changed; production setups need the separate installation guide
